questions.stem: A technician can reduce time near an ionizing radiation source, increase distance, or add shielding. Which planning approach is best?
options: Optimize all practical time, distance, and shielding measures to keep exposure as low as reasonably achievable while completing the task
Use only distance because time and shielding cannot be combined
Eliminate dosimetry whenever shielding is installed
Rely on the regulatory limit as the target exposure
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Radiation protection is layered. ALARA means planning to reduce dose through practical combinations rather than treating a limit as a desired exposure.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The option 'Use only distance because time and shielding cannot be combined' does not apply the controlling principle for time distance shielding to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

Share one badge among the crew because exposure is similar

questions.stem: A high-power laser beam crosses an occupied walkway at eye level. Operators wear eyewear, but there is no enclosure or interlock. What is the strongest control?

Enclose or terminate the beam path and use interlocks and controlled access, with suitable eyewear for residual exposure

questions.stem: At a dosimetry program audit, a supervisor proposes: "Use only distance because time and shielding cannot be combined". The underlying case is: A technician can reduce time near an ionizing radiation source, increase distance, or add shielding. Which planning approach is best? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Optimize all practical time, distance, and shielding measures to keep exposure as low as reasonably achievable while completing the task
Rely on the regulatory limit as the target exposure
Eliminate dosimetry whenever shielding is installed
Use only distance because time and shielding cannot be combined
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Radiation protection is layered. ALARA means planning to reduce dose through practical combinations rather than treating a limit as a desired exposure.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Rely on the regulatory limit as the target exposure' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling time distance shielding principle.
The proposed response 'Eliminate dosimetry whenever shielding is installed' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling time distance shielding principle.
The proposed response 'Use only distance because time and shielding cannot be combined' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling time distance shielding principle.

questions.stem: At a radioactive source inventory, a supervisor proposes: "320 mR/h". The underlying case is: A point-source exposure rate is 80 mR/h at 1 meter. Ignoring scatter and attenuation, what is the approximate rate at 4 meters? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: 20 mR/h
5 mR/h
320 mR/h
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: The distance increases by four, so intensity falls by 4² = 16: 80/16 = 5 mR/h.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response '20 mR/h' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling inverse square application principle.
The proposed response '320 mR/h' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling inverse square application principle.
The proposed response '1.25 mR/h' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling inverse square application principle.

questions.stem: At a UV exposure assessment, a supervisor proposes: "Share one badge among the crew because exposure is similar". The underlying case is: A worker wears a lead apron during fluoroscopic work. Where should dosimeters be placed when the program uses two badges to estimate whole-body exposure? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Share one badge among the crew because exposure is similar
Place both badges in a locker to avoid contaminating them
Place one badge outside the apron near the collar and one under the apron at the torso, following the facility’s approved dosimetry protocol
Wear both dosimeters together outside the apron so they provide duplicate readings from the same body location
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Two-badge protocols distinguish shielded torso dose from head and neck exposure. Exact placement follows the radiation safety program; badges must be individually assigned and worn.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Share one badge among the crew because exposure is similar' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling personal dosimetry placement principle.
The proposed response 'Place both badges in a locker to avoid contaminating them' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling personal dosimetry placement principle.

The proposed response 'Wear both dosimeters together outside the apron so they provide duplicate readings from the same body location' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling personal dosimetry placement principle.

questions.stem: At a time-distance-shielding decision, a supervisor proposes: "Treat every object exposed to a radiation field as permanently radioactive even when no radioactive material is deposited". The underlying case is: A sealed source passes near a workbench. Survey results show no radioactive material on the surface, but a worker asks whether the bench was “contaminated by radiation.” What is the correct explanation? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Treat every object exposed to a radiation field as permanently radioactive even when no radioactive material is deposited
Contamination and irradiation are interchangeable terms
A clean smear proves no radiation field ever existed
The bench may have been irradiated while the source was present, but contamination requires radioactive material to be deposited on it
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Irradiation is exposure to a field; contamination is unwanted radioactive material. A surface can be irradiated without retaining contamination or becoming activated.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Treat every object exposed to a radiation field as permanently radioactive even when no radioactive material is deposited' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling contamination versus irradiation principle.
The proposed response 'Contamination and irradiation are interchangeable terms' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling contamination versus irradiation principle.
The proposed response 'A clean smear proves no radiation field ever existed' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling contamination versus irradiation principle.

questions.stem: At a contamination control response, a supervisor proposes: "Wait for the next annual inventory before taking action". The underlying case is: A facility cannot locate one sealed source listed in its inventory. What is the appropriate response? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Initiate the license or program response for a missing source, secure areas, search and survey, notify required authorities, and investigate controls
Assume the source was disposed of with ordinary trash and close the issue
Delete the source from the inventory because it is no longer physically present
Wait for the next annual inventory before taking action
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Missing radioactive material is a security and exposure event requiring prompt controlled response and regulatory evaluation, not administrative deletion.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Assume the source was disposed of with ordinary trash and close the issue' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling source inventory and leak testing principle.
The proposed response 'Delete the source from the inventory because it is no longer physically present' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling source inventory and leak testing principle.
The proposed response 'Wait for the next annual inventory before taking action' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling source inventory and leak testing principle.

questions.stem: At an ionizing radiation work plan, a supervisor proposes: "Use darker eyewear without checking wavelength or optical density". The underlying case is: A high-power laser beam crosses an occupied walkway at eye level. Operators wear eyewear, but there is no enclosure or interlock. What is the strongest control? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Increase room lighting to neutralize laser energy
Enclose or terminate the beam path and use interlocks and controlled access, with suitable eyewear for residual exposure
Rely on warning signs because trained workers can avoid an invisible beam
Use darker eyewear without checking wavelength or optical density
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Laser safety prioritizes beam enclosure, termination, access control, and interlocks. Eyewear must be wavelength- and energy-appropriate and is not a substitute for engineering control.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Increase room lighting to neutralize laser energy' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling laser hazard controls principle.
The proposed response 'Rely on warning signs because trained workers can avoid an invisible beam' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling laser hazard controls principle.
The proposed response 'Use darker eyewear without checking wavelength or optical density' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling laser hazard controls principle.

questions.stem: At a laser safety review, a supervisor proposes: "Use ordinary clear spectacles regardless of UV transmission". The underlying case is: Workers use an intense UV curing source that can expose skin and eyes through a partially open housing. Which control is most effective? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Rely on the absence of visible brightness because UV is invisible
Apply sunscreen as the sole workplace control for eyes and skin
Complete the enclosure or interlock the access, control reflections, and provide wavelength-appropriate PPE for residual tasks
Use ordinary clear spectacles regardless of UV transmission
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: UV hazards require source enclosure, interlocks, reflection control, and suitable eye and skin protection. Visibility is not a reliable indicator of dose.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Rely on the absence of visible brightness because UV is invisible' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling ultraviolet exposure principle.
The proposed response 'Apply sunscreen as the sole workplace control for eyes and skin' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling ultraviolet exposure principle.
The proposed response 'Use ordinary clear spectacles regardless of UV transmission' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling ultraviolet exposure principle.

questions.stem: At a shielding calculation discussion, a supervisor proposes: "Increase survey speed so the detector covers more area". The underlying case is: A team must verify low-level removable beta contamination, but the available instrument has a thick window and poor beta response. What should they do? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Use the unsuitable instrument and interpret a zero reading as proof of no contamination
Increase survey speed so the detector covers more area
Measure room temperature and convert it to contamination level
Select and calibrate an instrument or sampling method suitable for the radiation type, energy, geometry, and required sensitivity
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Survey validity depends on detector response, window, geometry, calibration, background, and counting method. An insensitive detector can produce false reassurance.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Use the unsuitable instrument and interpret a zero reading as proof of no contamination' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling radiation survey instrument selection principle.
The proposed response 'Increase survey speed so the detector covers more area' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling radiation survey instrument selection principle.
The proposed response 'Measure room temperature and convert it to contamination level' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling radiation survey instrument selection principle.
